summary: Govind Chandra Pande (1923–2011) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. A former Vice Chancellor of the Universities of Rajasthan and Allahabad, he later chaired the Allahabad Museum around 1986 and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~1998–2004).

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (1893–1983) worked in Indology and other fields. After studying at Elphinstone College, he completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers (~1920–1922). He held a post at the University of Mumbai (~1924–1959).
Govind Sakharam Kathavate was an Indologist who succeeded Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar as the Sanskrit chair at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Govind Swamirao Gai (1917–1995) worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Succeeding Dineschandra Sircar, he served as Government Epigraphist and Chief Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), later consulting for the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who taught as a professor at Baroda College (attested 1933–1939). He later served as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist educated at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986) and later became associate professor and chair of East Asian Studies at McGill University around 1990.

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He earned his doctorate at Harvard University (~1972–1978) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and served as a lecturer at McMaster University from around 1978 to 2013.

Graham E. Clarke (d. 1998) worked in Tibetology and other fields. During his career, he held positions at the Institute of Development Studies and as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cambridge and LSE. He held positions at the University of Melbourne (~2001–2018), University of St Andrews (~2007–2018), and City University of New York (~2009).

Graves Champney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at East India Company College (~1814–1816), he succeeded Alexander Hamilton as Professor there (~1817–1827) and later served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University in 2002 under William C. Kirby, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Philip A. Kuhn, and later served as Associate Professor at Columbia University (attested 2008–2015).
Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist who founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano. In 1860, he became a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano.

Greg Bailey is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor J. Durham and teacher Madeleine Biardeau. He was later appointed to posts at La Trobe University, where he served as professor (attested 2004).

Gregor Ahn is a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit (~1985–1991) and later held an academic post at Heidelberg University around 2002.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under MA supervisor Helmut Tauscher (attested 2011), alongside training under several traditional teachers.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and Wolfson College, Oxford (D.Phil 2015), supervised by Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an Associate Professor of Japanese art and Buddhist visual cultures at UC Berkeley around 2002.

Gregory Schopen is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the Australian National University (~1975–1978). His faculty posts include Indiana University, University of Texas at Austin, Brown University, Stanford University, and UCLA.

Grigorij Maksimovič Bongard-Levin (1933–2008) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at MSU, he studied under George Roerich and held appointments at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Institute of World History.
